messages.text:
The remaining multi-directory diff is just the directory header path style: eza preserves the user’s slash style for `dir:` headers, but uses Windows-style basename joining for tree roots and direct file operands.

I’m separating those displays.

commands.commandLine:
"C:\\Program Files\\PowerShell\\7\\pwsh.exe" -Command "@'
import subprocess, pathlib
ref=pathlib.Path('REFERENCE_BINARY.txt').read_text().strip(); exe=str(pathlib.Path('executable.cmd').resolve())
cases=[
 ['tmp_probe','rust-reference/tests/itest','--color=never','--icons=never'],
 ['--long','tmp_probe','rust-reference/tests/itest','--color=never','--icons=never'],
 ['--tree','tmp_probe','rust-reference/tests/itest','--color=never','--icons=never'],
 ['tmp_probe/file10','tmp_probe/A.txt','--color=never','--icons=never'],
 ['--sort=size','tmp_probe/b.txt','tmp_probe/A.txt','--color=never','--icons=never'],
 ['no-such-file','--color=never','--icons=never'],
 ['--bad'],
 ['--sort=colour'],
]
for args in cases:
 r=subprocess.run([ref,*args],capture_output=True); p=subprocess.run([exe,*args],capture_output=True)
 ok=(r.returncode==p.returncode and r.stdout==p.stdout and (r.stderr==p.stderr or args[0]=='no-such-file'))
 print('OK' if ok else 'DIFF', args, r.returncode, p.returncode, len(r.stdout), len(p.stdout), len(r.stderr), len(p.stderr))
 if not ok:
  print('REF OUT', r.stdout[:1200].decode('utf-8','replace'))
  print('PY OUT', p.stdout[:1200].decode('utf-8','replace'))
  print('REF ERR', r.stderr.decode('utf-8','replace'))
  print('PY ERR', p.stderr.decode('utf-8','replace'))
  break
'@ | python -"
